_meta.what: The decision path per company: who owns, sponsors or vetoes a three-year sponsorship. See pipeline/intel/contacts.py for the shape and the rules.
_meta.rule: A person appears here ONLY when a real page names them in that role. If a company has no marketing officer, set no_cmo true and say so — never invent one.

companies.note: Full C-suite published on the company group team page. Marketing sits with a DACH-scoped CMO; a group-level 'Chief Marketing Officer (m/w/d)' req was also live on the company's join.com board, so the seat may be widening from DACH to group — worth re-checking before an approach.

people.name: Sophia Rödiger
people.note: The buyer for a Europe-facing FE programme. In seat since Aug 2023; profiled on 1KOMMA5°'s own magazine and speaking as CMO at HEROCON in June 2026. Ex-Daimler Mobility (digital strategy) and founder of bloXmove — automotive-adjacent, no direct motorsport tie found.

people.name: Sascha Koppe
people.note: Commercial owner across the group's country businesses.

people.name: Torben Diekmann
people.note: Growth remit sits alongside the CRO; relevant where a sponsorship is argued as customer acquisition rather than brand.

people.name: Philipp Schröder
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO. Was Chief Sales & Marketing Officer at Sonnen and Tesla's Germany country director — a founder who has personally run a marketing function, which matters for a brand-build pitch.

companies.note: Checked the company leadership page (antora.com/company): no CMO, VP Marketing or equivalent is listed. The nearest owner of external brand is Adam Frankel, VP Communications and Public Policy — an engineering- and policy-led company, so a sponsorship pitch runs through comms and the co-founder CCO, not a marketing department.

people.name: Adam Frankel
people.note: Closest thing to a marketing owner: holds brand, comms and policy. No CMO exists above him.

people.name: David Bierman
people.note: The real commercial decision-maker — fronts customers, utilities and financiers. Public speaker (Aspen Ideas) so used to platform appearances.

people.name: Andrew Ponec
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO.

companies.note: Checked the company site and careers board: no marketing officer of any level is named publicly. Base Power lists ~12 open Marketing & Community roles including an IC 'Growth Marketing' seat, so the function is being built but has no named head — the approach is Dell direct, or Pianta on the partnerships side.

people.name: Justin Lopas
people.note: Runs operations and build-out; ex-SpaceX and Anduril. No secondary company-page confirmation found for the title, hence reported.

people.name: Tim Pianta
people.note: Owns the partnership motion with utilities — the nearest existing partnerships seat in a company with no marketing head.

people.name: Zach Dell
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO. Cheque signer; company valued at $13bn after a $1bn Series D in Aug 2026.

companies.note: No sitting CMO is named publicly — the last announced CMO was Anthony Deighton in 2018. Marketing sits inside the President's remit: Celonis' own appointment release states Carsten Thoma is responsible for corporate strategy and development, MARKETING, platform ecosystem, culture and Celonis Labs. So the brief's named contact is, unusually, also the marketing owner.

people.name: Carsten Thoma
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still President (appointed Aug 2023; still listed as President on celonis.com/insights/authors/carsten-thoma). Marketing is explicitly in his brief, which makes him both the sponsorship buyer and a senior sponsor — the strongest single entry point of the eleven. Co-founder of Hybris, first external investor in Celonis.

people.name: Miguel Milano
people.note: Owns worldwide revenue; co-owner stake makes him a veto as well as a buyer.

people.name: Alexander Rinke
people.note: Co-CEO with Bastian Nominacher; Munich-headquartered, which fits a European FE calendar.

companies.note: The only company in this batch whose brief already names the marketing owner, and it checks out. Full leadership published at databricks.com/company/leadership-team; EMEA is a named region with its own GM, which matters for a Formula E calendar weighted to Europe and the Middle East.

people.name: Rick Schultz
people.note: Brief's named contact and correct: CMO since 2017, still in seat in 2026. Owns product marketing, demand gen, brand and creative, global comms, events and field marketing — a sponsorship lands squarely in his budget. Ex-SVP Marketing at Alteryx, ex-Oracle.

people.name: Ron Gabrisko
people.note: Worldwide sales and go-to-market; the co-signer on anything pitched as pipeline rather than brand.

people.name: Samuel Bonamigo
people.note: Runs EMEA and was still referenced in that role in the Sep 2025 Benelux/Nordics appointment release — the regional budget holder for European race weekends.

people.name: Ali Ghodsi
people.note: Cheque signer at the top of a company of this size; realistically a ratifier, not the entry point.

companies.note: Checked emeraldai.co/team and emeraldai.co/company: no CMO, VP Marketing or comms lead is listed. A ~2-year-old, research-led company (founded 2024) — the sponsorship conversation is with Sivaram directly, with Padilla as the commercial operator. Do not expect a marketing budget line to exist yet.

people.name: Daniel Padilla
people.role: Chief of Staff & Director, Commercial Strategy & Operations
people.note: The commercial operator around the CEO; joined from Rondo Energy. In a company this size, the practical route to Sivaram's diary.

people.name: Dr. Varun Sivaram
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still Founder & CEO. Ex-Chief Strategy & Innovation Officer at Ørsted and ex-CTO of ReNew Power — an unusually brand-literate energy executive, and the person who would personally decide a sponsorship.

people.name: Prof. Ayse Coskun
people.note: Academic authority on orchestrating data-centre power demand for grid response — the technical counterpart if the pitch is an energy-flexibility workstream with a team's operations rather than a logo.

companies.note: One of only three companies in this batch with a real CMO in seat. EnergyX publishes its executive leadership on energyx.com, and Khalil is named on 2026 press releases (Project Lonestar, the Eni $225M investment, the nuclear-materials platform) — an active, well-funded brand-building programme to sell into.

people.name: Kellee Khalil
people.note: The buyer. Owns business, brand and marketing strategy; with the company since inception and still named on 2026 releases. A serial entrepreneur and brand builder — the profile that responds to a sponsorship narrative rather than a media schedule.

people.name: Chloe Ke
people.role: Executive Vice President, Strategy and Sales
people.note: Nearest thing to a commercial officer — strategy and sales in one seat.

people.name: Teague Egan
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still Founder, Chairman & CEO. Founder-controlled, so he is both cheque signer and veto.

people.name: Amit Patwardhan
people.note: Technical counterpart for any battery-materials or lithium-chemistry workstream with a race team.

companies.note: Checked the management team page on Fervo's investor site (now NASDAQ: FRVO): no CMO or VP Marketing is listed. Communications sits inside the COO's remit — Fervo's own June 2026 release naming Sarah Jewett COO lists supply chain, land, permitting, policy, communications, strategy and people operations under her. So the marketing owner here is the COO, and a public-company disclosure discipline now applies to anything announced.

people.name: Sarah Jewett
people.note: The nearest buyer: communications is explicitly in her remit and no marketing officer exists above her. Newly promoted (10 June 2026) — a fresh mandate is a good moment to land a three-year proposal. Ex-Select Energy Services corporate development, ex-Schlumberger engineer.

people.name: Dawn Owens
people.role: SVP, Head of Development & Commercial Markets
people.note: Owns development and commercial markets since 2020; the counterpart if the pitch is framed around customer and offtake audiences.

people.name: Tim Latimer
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO and a director since 2018. Now runs a listed company, so a sponsorship needs a stated commercial rationale, not a founder's enthusiasm.

companies.note: Checked formenergy.com/about and the team pages: no CMO or VP Marketing. External voice sits with Sarah Bray, VP Communications; the commercial owner is RJ Johnson, SVP Commercial Operations. Engineering- and utility-led, so pitch the sponsorship to Johnson as a utility-audience platform and to Bray as brand.

people.name: Sarah Bray
people.note: Closest to a marketing owner; no CMO exists above her. Title confirmed only via secondary listings of the company team page, hence reported.

people.name: RJ Johnson
people.note: The real commercial decision-maker: utility, commercial and residential storage markets. Has his own page on the company team site.

people.name: Mateo Jaramillo
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still Co-Founder & CEO. Built and ran Tesla's stationary storage business before Form — an automotive-adjacent history that gives a motorsport conversation a foothold.

people.name: Ted Wiley
people.note: President/COO-level co-founder; the second signature on anything multi-year.

companies.note: Checked gatik.ai's about and press-release pages: no CMO, VP Marketing or brand lead is named. The external-facing seat is Richard Steiner (VP, Government Relations & Public Affairs, previously head of policy and communications) and the buyer of a partnership is Paul DiLaura, the Chief Commercial Officer. Gatik's May 2025 leadership build-out added a CFO and a Chief Legal Officer but no marketing officer.

people.name: Richard Steiner
people.role: Vice President, Government Relations & Public Affairs
people.note: Owns policy and public affairs and previously headed policy and communications; the closest thing to a brand owner in a company with no marketing officer. Fronts broadcast appearances (NBC Today Show).

people.name: Paul DiLaura
people.note: In the absence of a CMO, the practical buyer — owns customer-facing commercial strategy and is the company's public commercial voice through 2026 (ACT Expo, freight podcasts).

people.name: Gautam Narang
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO & Co-Founder.

people.name: Arjun Narang
people.note: Technical counterpart for an autonomy/logistics workstream around a race team's freight and paddock operations.

companies.note: Enterprise-AI company with a full go-to-market bench. Arvind Jain is confirmed still Founder & CEO, but he is not the sponsorship buyer — Matt Kixmoeller owns the global marketing organisation and is the call to make. No CRO is listed; worldwide sales sits with an SVP.

people.name: Matt Kixmoeller
people.note: Owns the global marketing organisation — the sponsorship buyer. Joined from self-driving software company Ghost Autonomy; before that a founding marketing leader at Pure Storage, where he helped define the all-flash array category. A category-creation marketer, which is the profile that buys a multi-year series platform rather than a logo.

people.name: Marc Wendling
people.note: Appointed in Glean's own press release explicitly to drive global expansion beyond the US — the commercial counterpart for an EMEA-weighted Formula E platform. Glean lists no CRO; this is the senior revenue seat.

people.name: Juliet Bramwell
people.note: Runs EMEA out of Glean's London operations and R&D hub, with customers including Booking.com, GSK and Ericsson and a stated push into Germany, France, Italy and Spain — the same map as the Formula E calendar. Joined from Google Cloud after nine years. Named in trade press rather than on Glean's own site; the company is separately advertising a Regional VP Sales EMEA role, so confirm the structure before the desk calls.

people.name: Arvind Jain
people.note: The brief's named decision-maker — confirmed still Founder & CEO. Ex-Google Distinguished Engineer, co-founder of Rubrik. Cheque signer, not the buyer.

people.name: Tamar Yehoshua
people.note: Runs product and engineering; the counterpart if the Mahindra play is a real deployed-search workstream rather than a halo. Former Chief Product Officer at Slack and a product leader at Google. Title read from secondary coverage of Glean's about page rather than a page I could open directly — re-confirm before it goes in a brief.

companies.note: CORRECTION FOR THE DESK: the brief names 'Mark Seeger — Founder & Co-CEO'. Glydways' own about page and leadership bios now name Gokul Hemmady as CEO (he joined in 2019 as President & CFO); Seeger is described as founder, and secondary sources report he has moved to Chief Strategy Officer. There is a dedicated marketing owner, but no C-level CMO: the senior marketing seat is a VP of Marketing & Communications, and commercial ownership sits with the CCO, whose own remit explicitly covers strategic partnerships.

people.name: Kim Jennett
people.note: Senior-most marketing owner at Glydways; no CMO is listed on the leadership page or the 2025 leadership-bios PDF.

people.name: Chris Riley
people.note: The company's own bios describe the CCO as responsible for growing global business, strategic partnerships and corporate reputation — i.e. the seat a sponsorship would actually sit in. The company page carries the first name only; the surname is confirmed against his LinkedIn profile, so treat the full name as reported.

people.name: Amair Saleem
people.role: Managing Director, Transport Middle East & Senior Vice President, Operational Readiness
people.note: Runs the Middle East. 35+ years in transit systems and urban air mobility; relevant because the Gulf rounds are where a transport-infrastructure brand gets host-market value.

people.name: Gokul Hemmady
people.note: Current CEO, joined 2019 as President & CFO. Replaces the brief's out-of-date 'Mark Seeger, Founder & Co-CEO'.

companies.note: Marketing is owned by a VP, not a CMO: Chris Churilo is named as the company media contact on every groundcover press release from Oct 2025 through May 2026. No public sales/revenue officer — the sponsorship route is Churilo, with Azulay as cheque signer after the $100M Series C (Jul 2026).

people.name: Chris Churilo
people.note: The buyer. Named as groundcover's media contact (chris.churilo@groundcover.com) on company-issued releases from Oct 2025 to May 2026 — owns brand and demand gen for a company that has just raised to build a Datadog challenger.

people.name: Shahar Azulay
people.note: Brief's named contact, confirmed still CEO — quoted as co-founder & CEO in the July 2026 Series C release ($100M at a ~$500M valuation).

people.name: Yechezkel Rabinovich
people.note: Technical counterpart for any telemetry/observability workstream with a race team; ex-cyber unit, Israeli PM's Office, with Azulay.

companies.note: Checked Helion's own team page (helionenergy.com/who-we-are) and about page: no CMO, no marketing or commercial officer is listed. Engineering-led, and the only named commercial-adjacent function found in secondary sources is a Director of Communications, which is below the bar for this record. The buyer here is effectively the CEO plus the executive chairman.

people.name: David Kirtley
people.note: The brief's named decision-maker — confirmed still Founder & CEO. With no marketing officer in place, he is both buyer and cheque signer.

people.name: Sam Altman
people.note: Executive chairman and a major backer; on a discretionary multi-year brand commitment at a pre-revenue fusion company, he is a real veto point, not a figurehead.

people.name: Chris Pihl
people.note: Helion's own pages confirm him as a co-founder; the CTO title comes from secondary profiles only. Technical counterpart if an Envision play is built on real energy hardware rather than a halo.

companies.note: Checked Hydrostor's own company page and its executive-appointment press releases: no CMO or marketing officer. The commercial owner is the CCO, and the company has built out C-suite depth (CFO, CTO, CDO, CHRO, EVP Policy) without adding a marketing seat — so a sponsorship pitch lands with commercial, not brand.

people.name: Jordan Cole
people.note: Senior-most buyer in the absence of a CMO; owns commercial strategy across a project pipeline the company puts above 6 GW / 65 GWh.

people.name: Curtis VanWalleghem
people.note: The brief's named decision-maker — confirmed still Co-Founder & CEO. Ex-Deloitte corporate strategy, Bruce Power.

people.name: Chris Phebus
people.note: Named in Hydrostor's own appointment release; the counterpart for any Andretti energy-storage or paddock-power workstream.

companies.note: The cleanest decision path in this batch: at Infineon the CMO is a Management Board seat, so marketing ownership and cheque-signing authority sit at the same table. The brief's named decision-maker is correct and his mandate runs to 2030.

people.name: Andreas Urschitz
people.role: Chief Marketing Officer, Member of the Management Board
people.note: The brief's named decision-maker — confirmed. Management Board member and CMO since 2022; the Supervisory Board extended his contract for five years to 31 May 2030, so he owns the whole life of a three-year deal. Previously President of the Power & Sensor Systems division; with Infineon since 1995.

people.name: Jochen Hanebeck
people.note: CEO since 2022, on the Management Board since 2016. Sponsor for a group-level brand commitment; Infineon reorganised into three segments (Automotive, Power Systems, Edge Systems) from Q4 FY2026, and Automotive is the segment a Jaguar TCS platform speaks to.

companies.note: Lime IPO'd in mid-2026 and the investor-relations management team page carries no CMO — the first-CMO appointment (Duke Stump, 2020) is no longer on the roster. Brand and communications now sit inside the Chief Business Officer's remit, which is where a sponsorship decision would be taken. Wayne Ting is confirmed still CEO.

people.name: David Spielfogel
people.note: The marketing owner by remit rather than title: Lime's own filing-grade bio says he oversees global government relations, business development, communications and brand. In post since February 2023. THE call for Envision — brand plus city/government relations in one seat, which matters for a London-based FE platform.

people.name: Kaan Taş
people.note: The current UK regional owner and the most useful local seat for an Envision Racing play — Envision is a London team and Lime's UK book is its European showcase. Reports 5x growth in the region in three years; previously scaled operations at OYO. Named in 2025-26 conference speaker bios rather than on Lime's own site: Lime's post-IPO IR roster lists C-suite only, no regional GMs. An earlier company blog post named Marek Łusiak as Regional GM EMEA across 11 countries, but that post dates from 2021-22 and could not be re-confirmed, so it is not carried here.

people.name: Wayne Ting
people.note: The brief's named decision-maker — confirmed still CEO, in post since May 2020 and a board member. Now signing as a public-company CEO, so a discretionary multi-year spend carries added disclosure scrutiny.

companies.note: Checked Moove's own about and careers pages: they name the two co-founders and describe a Co-CEO/President structure, but no marketing officer is named anywhere on the company's own site — the most senior marketing role advertised is a country-level Marketing Manager. Treat the co-founders as the buyers. Newly valued at c.$2.1bn after a $250m Series C led by Mubadala, and a Waymo fleet partner, so the capital is there; the marketing function is not yet built out.

people.name: Tingting Peng
people.note: Moove's first executive hire (early 2021) and the senior non-founder commercial seat; a practical entry point when the co-CEOs are unreachable. Named only in investor/secondary coverage, not on Moove's own site.

people.name: Jide Odunsi
people.note: The brief's other named decision-maker — confirmed. Ex-Goldman Sachs banker and ex-McKinsey consultant; LSE and MIT Sloan. The finance-side co-CEO, so the one to convince on a three-year committed spend.

people.name: Ladi Delano
people.note: One of the brief's two named decision-makers — confirmed. British-born Nigerian entrepreneur with prior founder exits in Africa and Asia; Master's from Oxford, MPA from LSE. With no CMO, he is the buyer as well as the signer.

companies.note: MOTORSPORT / MAJOR-SPORT TIE FOUND — and it is the strongest commercial signal in this batch. Octopus already buys elite sport: its longest-standing partnership is with Arsenal FC, a purpose-led green-energy tie-up recognised by the European Sponsorship Association, and it runs grassroots football activation (free kits for 500 children's teams). No motorsport sponsorship found — Octopus is not on the Formula E partner list — so the category lane is open, and the buying committee has already proven it will commit to a multi-year sport platform on a sustainability thesis. Marketing is run entirely in-house, which means the pitch goes to the CPMO directly, not through an agency.

people.name: Rebecca Dibb-Simkin
people.note: THE call. Group CPMO and the owner of the sponsorship budget — she runs product and marketing as one function on the stated principle that the two should never be split, with all marketing done in-house (design, copy and booking sitting alongside operations). Joined as employee #43 in 2016 and scaled the group to 32 countries. Previously eight years at British Gas, where she led the product team that took Hive to the UK's leading smart-home brand.

people.name: Greg Jackson
people.note: The brief's named decision-maker — confirmed still Founder & CEO. Serial tech entrepreneur with prior businesses built and sold; a high-visibility public advocate for the group, which makes him a genuine sponsor for a brand-led play rather than a rubber stamp.

companies.note: A full consumer-brand buying committee: CMO for brand, CCO for the commercial and partnership side. Note the CMO seat turned over — the desk should not still be carrying Oura's first CMO.

people.name: Doug Sweeny
people.note: Current CMO and the buyer. Succeeded Karina Kogan, Oura's first-ever CMO, who moved to an advisory role supporting strategic partnerships — so any older record naming Kogan as CMO is stale.

people.name: Dorothy Kilroy
people.note: Oura's first-ever CCO, announced by the company. The counterpart for the athlete-data and team-performance side of an Andretti play, where the product is worn rather than badged.

people.name: Tom Hale
people.note: The brief's named decision-maker — confirmed still CEO.

companies.note: Engineering-led and young (founded 2023): checked the company's own mission/team page and no CMO or marketing officer is listed — the named seats are CEO, President and Chief Nuclear Officer. Capital is not the constraint (a $1bn Series B led by Sequoia, and selection for the President's Accelerated Nuclear Program), but there is no marketing function to buy a sponsorship, so the path runs founder → President.

people.name: Muhammad Shahzad
people.note: The company's team page lists a President seat; the name comes from secondary company profiles rather than a page I could open, so confirm the spelling before use. In a founder-led company with no marketing officer, the President is the practical commercial entry point.

people.name: Isaiah Taylor
people.note: The brief's named decision-maker — confirmed still Founder & CEO. Founded the company in 2023; self-taught engineer who left school at 16. With no CMO, he is the buyer.

people.name: Mark Mitchell
people.note: Leads the technical effort. Previously president of modular-reactor firm Ultra Safe Nuclear Corporation and led the world's first small modular reactor project at South Africa's Pebble Bed Modular Reactor; 25 years in energy. Name and background from secondary coverage of the company's team page.

companies.note: MOTORSPORT TIE FOUND — Zenobē has already sponsored electric racing: it partnered with Extreme E to power the series' paddock using second-life batteries, on an explicit shared-electrification thesis. That is a company that has bought motorsport before, on exactly the technical-workstream logic a Jaguar TCS play would use, and it is not currently on the Formula E partner list. Also new for the desk: the brief carries NO named decision-maker for Zenobē, and there now is one — Dr Donald Weir became CEO, working alongside the two remaining founder directors. No CMO or marketing officer is listed on the leadership page; commercial ownership sits with regional presidents. Third co-founder Nicholas Beatty has retired from the business.

people.name: Ruben Benders
people.note: The practical buyer in the absence of a CMO. Leads commercial activity for electric truck and bus fleet charging across Germany, Spain, Benelux and beyond, and owns go-to-market for continental Europe — which maps directly onto the European weighting of the Formula E calendar. 25+ years in the energy transition across power, gas and CO2 trading and heavy-duty EV charging.

people.name: Donald Weir
people.note: Fills the gap the brief left blank. Announced by Zenobē as CEO, working alongside the two founders across their respective business areas; 20+ years of global leadership with senior roles at Siemens, E.ON and thyssenkrupp. An industrial-utility CEO, so the case has to be built on grid and fleet outcomes, not on halo.

people.name: Steven Meersman
people.note: One of the two remaining founder directors (with James Basden) after Nicholas Beatty's retirement. Founder directors run their own business areas alongside the CEO, so a group brand commitment needs them on side.
